citation.title: Phased LSTM: Accelerating Recurrent Network Training for Long or Event-based Sequences
citation.authors: D. Neil, M. Pfeiffer, S.-C. Liu
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 29 (NIPS 2016)

topic: LSTM variant with a learned oscillatory time gate for irregularly sampled, event-driven, or multi-rate inputs
own_question: Can a time-gated LSTM handle asynchronous or multi-rate sequences and train faster on long sequences?
actual_method_and_evidence: Adds a periodic time gate with learned period and phase. Tested on synthetic sine-frequency discrimination, the adding task, N-MNIST event-camera data, and GRID audio-video lip reading. These are ML benchmarks only, with no plasma or diagnostic data.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Recurrent architectures have been proposed for irregularly sampled inputs and for fusing sensors with different sampling rates.
claim_checks.qualification: Applies only to a generic ML method on non-fusion benchmarks. It is not a tested estimator for CES nowcasting.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Input timestamps drive the gate. The source does not address report latency or nowcasting of the current label.
validation_if_relevant: Some benchmarks report means over 5 seeds, but the source has no plasma validation and its split details are only partial.
forbidden_inferences: that its 5% compute reduction or accuracy transfers to our task
that it gives real-time plasma capability
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Cite at most in one sentence on multi-rate or irregular sequence models in related work. Excluding it is reasonable because we did not use this model.
